import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem in sub-exponential time

Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, let $P \in E(\mathbb{F}_q)$
and let $Q$ be in the cyclic subgroup generated by $P$. The *discrete logarithm problem* on $E$
asks for an integer $k$ with $Q = kP$. The best known classical algorithms for a general elliptic
curve (baby-step giant-step, Pollard's rho) run in time about $\sqrt{q} = 2^{\Theta(\log q)}$,
which is exponential in the input size $\Theta(\log q)$.

Wikipedia asks: *Can a discrete logarithm on an elliptic curve be computed in sub-exponential
time?*

We formalise this as the existence of a deterministic Turing machine (the `TM2` model of
`Mathlib.Computability.TMComputable`, as in `FormalConjectures/Millenium/PvsNP.lean`) that
solves the discrete logarithm problem on every elliptic curve over every finite field within
$2^{o(n)}$ steps, where $n$ is the length of the input. Finite fields are presented as
$\mathbb{F}_p[X]/(f)$ with $f$ monic irreducible, curves by a Weierstrass equation, and the input
is a fixed binary encoding of all this data, so that $n = \Theta(\log q)$.

Randomised algorithms with expected running time bounds, which the cryptographic literature
often allows, are not modelled; only the worst-case running time of deterministic classical
machines is considered. Quantum algorithms are not covered.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Discrete logarithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/discrete_logarithm)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Elliptic-curve cryptography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elliptic-curve_cryptography)
-/
open Computability Turing Polynomial Filter
namespace DiscreteLogarithm2

structure Input where
  /-- The characteristic of the finite field. -/
  p : ℕ
  [hp : Fact p.Prime]
  /-- The monic irreducible polynomial `f` presenting the finite field `𝔽_p[X]/(f)`. -/
  f : (ZMod p)[X]
  monic : f.Monic
  [irreducible : Fact (Irreducible f)]
  /-- The elliptic curve, given by a Weierstrass equation over `𝔽_p[X]/(f)`. -/
  E : WeierstrassCurve (AdjoinRoot f)
  [elliptic : E.IsElliptic]
  /-- The base point. -/
  P : E.toAffine.Point
  /-- The point whose discrete logarithm with respect to `P` is sought. -/
  Q : E.toAffine.Point
blocks.docstring:
An input to the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem. It consists of
- a prime `p`,
- a monic irreducible polynomial `f` over `𝔽_p = ZMod p`, presenting the finite field
  `𝔽_q = 𝔽_p[X]/(f) = AdjoinRoot f` with `q = p ^ deg f`,
- an elliptic curve `E` over `𝔽_q`, given by a (long) Weierstrass equation,
- two points `P` and `Q` of `E(𝔽_q)`.

Every finite field, and every elliptic curve over it, arises this way up to isomorphism.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Quantifying directly with ∀ binders over `WeierstrassCurve (GaloisField p n)`; rejected because `GaloisField` has no concrete element representation to encode, and a structure keeps the statement readable.
justification.name: DiscreteLogarithm2.Input
justification.why_needed: Bundles an instance of the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem over an arbitrary finite field: prime p, monic irreducible f over ZMod p, elliptic Weierstrass curve E over AdjoinRoot f, points P, Q. Needed so that the algorithm is quantified over all such instances with a single concrete encoding.

blocks.text:
/--
An input to the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem. It consists of
- a prime `p`,
- a monic irreducible polynomial `f` over `𝔽_p = ZMod p`, presenting the finite field
  `𝔽_q = 𝔽_p[X]/(f) = AdjoinRoot f` with `q = p ^ deg f`,
- an elliptic curve `E` over `𝔽_q`, given by a (long) Weierstrass equation,
- two points `P` and `Q` of `E(𝔽_q)`.

Every finite field, and every elliptic curve over it, arises this way up to isomorphism.
-/
structure Input where
  /-- The characteristic of the finite field. -/
  p : ℕ
  [hp : Fact p.Prime]
  /-- The monic irreducible polynomial `f` presenting the finite field `𝔽_p[X]/(f)`. -/

  monic : f.Monic
  [irreducible : Fact (Irreducible f)]
  /-- The elliptic curve, given by a Weierstrass equation over `𝔽_p[X]/(f)`. -/
  E : WeierstrassCurve (AdjoinRoot f)
  [elliptic : E.IsElliptic]
  /-- The base point. -/
  P : E.toAffine.Point
  /-- The point whose discrete logarithm with respect to `P` is sought. -/
  Q : E.toAffine.Point
attribute [instance] Input.hp Input.irreducible Input.elliptic

noncomputable def encodeElem (x : AdjoinRoot I.f) : List ℕ :=
  (List.range I.f.natDegree).map fun i => ((AdjoinRoot.modByMonicHom I.monic x).coeff i).val
blocks.docstring:
The list of the `deg f` coefficients, as natural numbers `< p`, of the unique representative of
degree `< deg f` of an element of `𝔽_p[X]/(f)`.

/--
The list of natural numbers describing an input: the prime `p`, the degree `n` of `f`, the `n`

def encodeNatList (l : List ℕ) : List Γ' :=
  (l.map fun k => (encodeNat k).map Γ'.bit ++ [Γ'.comma]).flatten
blocks.docstring:

each number in binary (via `Computability.encodeNat`, least significant bit first) followed by a
`comma`.

def IsSubexponential (T : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (T n : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ (ε * n)
blocks.docstring:
A time bound `T : ℕ → ℕ` is *sub-exponential* if `T n = 2 ^ o(n)`, that is, if for every
`ε > 0` we have `T n ≤ 2 ^ (ε * n)` for all sufficiently large `n`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime` (polynomial only) and `Asymptotics.IsLittleO` (would need composition with log; the ε-formulation is more transparent).
justification.name: DiscreteLogarithm2.IsSubexponential
justification.why_needed: The notion `T n = 2^{o(n)}` of a subexponential time bound; not present in Mathlib or the repo.

blocks.name: IsSubexponential
blocks.text:
/--
A time bound `T : ℕ → ℕ` is *sub-exponential* if `T n = 2 ^ o(n)`, that is, if for every
`ε > 0` we have `T n ≤ 2 ^ (ε * n)` for all sufficiently large `n`.
-/
def IsSubexponential (T : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (T n : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ (ε * n)

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 68]
theorem isSubexponential_pow (d : ℕ) : IsSubexponential fun n => n ^ d := by
  intro ε hε
  have h := isLittleO_pow_exp_pos_mul_atTop d (mul_pos hε (Real.log_pos one_lt_two))
  filter_upwards [tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop.eventually (h.bound one_pos)] with n hn
  simp only [Real.norm_eq_abs, one_mul, abs_pow, Nat.abs_cast] at hn
  push_cast
  calc (n : ℝ) ^ d ≤ |Real.exp (ε * Real.log 2 * n)| := hn
    _ = 2 ^ (ε * n) := by
      rw [abs_of_pos (Real.exp_pos _), Real.rpow_def_of_pos two_pos]
      ring_nf

/-- Polynomial time bounds are sub-exponential. -/

theorem isSubexponential_pow (d : ℕ) : IsSubexponential fun n => n ^ d := by

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 68]
theorem not_isSubexponential_two_pow : ¬ IsSubexponential fun n => 2 ^ n := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := (h (1 / 2) (by norm_num)).exists_forall_of_atTop
  have h1 := hN (N + 1) (by omega)
  have h2 : ((2 : ℝ) ^ ((1 / 2 : ℝ) * ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ))) < 2 ^ ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) :=
    Real.rpow_lt_rpow_of_exponent_lt one_lt_two (by push_cast; linarith)
  rw [Real.rpow_natCast] at h2
  push_cast at h1 h2
  linarith
blocks.docstring: The exponential time bound `2 ^ n` is not sub-exponential.

@[category research open, AMS 11 14 68]
theorem discrete_logarithm_2 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (M : TM2ComputableAux Γ' Γ') (T : ℕ → ℕ), IsSubexponential T ∧
      ∀ I : Input, (∃ k : ℕ, I.Q = k • I.P) → ∃ k : ℕ, I.Q = k • I.P ∧
        Nonempty (TM2OutputsInTime M.tm (I.encode.map M.inputAlphabet.symm)
          (some (((encodeNat k).map Γ'.bit).map M.outputAlphabet.symm)) (T I.encode.length)) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Elliptic curve discrete logarithms in sub-exponential time.**

Can a discrete logarithm on an elliptic curve be computed in sub-exponential time?

That is, is there a deterministic Turing machine `M` and a sub-exponential time bound
`T n = 2 ^ o(n)` such that for every prime `p`, every finite field `𝔽_q = 𝔽_p[X]/(f)` with `f`
monic irreducible, every elliptic curve `E` over `𝔽_q` given by a Weierstrass equation and all
points `P`, `Q` of `E(𝔽_q)` with `Q` in the subgroup generated by `P`, the machine `M`, started
on the binary encoding of `(p, f, E, P, Q)`, halts within `T (input length)` steps and outputs
the binary encoding of a natural number `k` with `Q = k • P`?

The input length is `Θ(log q)`, so the generic algorithms, which take about `√q` steps, are
exponential. Only the worst-case running time of deterministic (classical) machines is
considered; randomised algorithms are not modelled, and Shor's algorithm solves the problem in
polynomial time on a quantum computer.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (answer(sorry) : Prop): does there exist a classical (non-quantum, since Shor gives polynomial-time quantum) algorithm that, given an elliptic curve over an arbitrary finite field, a point P and a point Q in ⟨P⟩, outputs k with Q = kP in time 2^{o(n)} where n is the input bit-length (≈ log of the field size / group order); the algorithm must work for all curves (not just special families like supersingular or anomalous curves, which already have subexponential attacks), and the literature's default of allowing randomized/expected running time and the choice of computation model (e.g. Turing machines as in Millenium/PvsNP.lean) are conventions the formalizer must fix explicitly.
claims.reviewer_why: c06 states the promise problem literally, as the decomposition describes it: one deterministic Mathlib `FinTM2` machine M and one bound T with T = 2^{o(n)} such that, for every prime p, every finite field F_p[X]/(f) (f monic irreducible; every finite field arises this way), every elliptic curve E (long Weierstrass equation with `IsElliptic`, so char 2 and 3 are covered) and all points P, Q with Q ∈ ⟨P⟩, M started on a canonical binary encoding of (p, f, E, P, Q) (length Θ(log q)) halts within T(n) steps with the binary encoding of some k with Q = k • P. answer(True) is a positive answer; the quantifier structure is `∀ I, (∃ k, …) → ∃ k, … ∧ …` (not the trivial `∃ x, P x → Q` form); the statement is not vacuous (Input is nonempty) and not trivially true (generic algorithms are 2^{Θ(n)}). It also includes API tests for its bespoke definitions (encoding examples, polynomial bounds are subexponential, 2^n is not). c03/c04/c05/c08 are also sound but use `TM2ComputableInTime`, which additionally requires the machine to halt within T(n) on every (including malformed / non-promise) input — a standard but extra convention that is not literally in the source and can differ in pathological cases from the promise-only reading; they also admit non-reduced input representatives. c07 is equivalent to c06 in content (abstract finite field with a PowerBasis) but has no tests for its bespoke definitions. My edits to c06: tests moved next to the definitions they test, docstrings tightened and made explicit that randomised/expected-time algorithms are not modelled.

context:
In mathematics, for given real numbers $a$ and $b$, the logarithm $\log _{b}(a)$ is a number $x$ such that $b^{x}=a$. The discrete logarithm is an analogous concept in group theory. In any group $G$, powers $b^{k}$ can be defined for all integers $k$, and the discrete logarithm $\log _{b}(a)$ is an integer $k$ such that $b^{k}=a$. In the special case of arithmetic modulo an integer $m$, the more commonly used term is index: One can write $k=\operatorname {ind} _{b}a\!\!\!\!{\pmod {m}}$ when $b^{k}\equiv a\!\!\!\!{\pmod {m}}$.
Discrete logarithms are quickly computable in a few special cases, but no efficient method is known for computing them in general. Several cryptographic systems, including Diffie–Hellman and ElGamal, base their security on the hardness assumption that the discrete logarithm problem over carefully chosen groups has no efficient solution. In general, there is no subexponential time solution for black box groups.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single slot is a yes/no question and is formalized as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ algorithm`. As the table's notes anticipate, the conventions (deterministic vs randomized, computation model, exact meaning of subexponential, input encoding) had to be fixed; they are recorded in modeling_decisions and in the theorem docstring. The randomized-algorithm reading could not be offered as a variant because no probabilistic computation primitives exist in Mathlib.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem in sub-exponential time

Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, let $P \in E(\mathbb{F}_q)$
and let $Q$ be in the cyclic subgroup generated by $P$. The *discrete logarithm problem* on $E$
asks for an integer $k$ with $Q = kP$. The best known classical algorithms for a general elliptic
curve (baby-step giant-step, Pollard's rho) run in time about $\sqrt{q} = 2^{\Theta(\log q)}$,
which is exponential in the input size $\Theta(\log q)$.

Wikipedia asks: *Can a discrete logarithm on an elliptic curve be computed in sub-exponential
time?*

We formalise this as the existence of a deterministic Turing machine (the `TM2` model of
`Mathlib.Computability.TMComputable`, as in `FormalConjectures/Millenium/PvsNP.lean`) that
solves the discrete logarithm problem on every elliptic curve over every finite field within
$2^{o(n)}$ steps, where $n$ is the length of the input. Finite fields are presented as
$\mathbb{F}_p[X]/(f)$ with $f$ monic irreducible, curves by a Weierstrass equation, and the input
is a fixed binary encoding of all this data, so that $n = \Theta(\log q)$.

Randomised algorithms with expected running time bounds, which the cryptographic literature
often allows, are not modelled; only the worst-case running time of deterministic classical
machines is considered. Quantum algorithms are not covered.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Discrete logarithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/discrete_logarithm)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Elliptic-curve cryptography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elliptic-curve_cryptography)
-/

open Computability Turing Polynomial Filter

namespace DiscreteLogarithm2

/--
An input to the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem. It consists of
- a prime `p`,
- a monic irreducible polynomial `f` over `𝔽_p = ZMod p`, presenting the finite field
  `𝔽_q = 𝔽_p[X]/(f) = AdjoinRoot f` with `q = p ^ deg f`,
- an elliptic curve `E` over `𝔽_q`, given by a (long) Weierstrass equation,
- two points `P` and `Q` of `E(𝔽_q)`.

Every finite field, and every elliptic curve over it, arises this way up to isomorphism.
-/
structure Input where
  /-- The characteristic of the finite field. -/
  p : ℕ
  [hp : Fact p.Prime]
  /-- The monic irreducible polynomial `f` presenting the finite field `𝔽_p[X]/(f)`. -/
  f : (ZMod p)[X]
  monic : f.Monic
  [irreducible : Fact (Irreducible f)]
  /-- The elliptic curve, given by a Weierstrass equation over `𝔽_p[X]/(f)`. -/
  E : WeierstrassCurve (AdjoinRoot f)
  [elliptic : E.IsElliptic]
  /-- The base point. -/
  P : E.toAffine.Point
  /-- The point whose discrete logarithm with respect to `P` is sought. -/
  Q : E.toAffine.Point

attribute [instance] Input.hp Input.irreducible Input.elliptic

namespace Input

variable (I : Input)

/--
The list of the `deg f` coefficients, as natural numbers `< p`, of the unique representative of
degree `< deg f` of an element of `𝔽_p[X]/(f)`.
-/
noncomputable def encodeElem (x : AdjoinRoot I.f) : List ℕ :=
  (List.range I.f.natDegree).map fun i => ((AdjoinRoot.modByMonicHom I.monic x).coeff i).val

/--
A point of `E(𝔽_q)` is encoded by the tag `0` if it is the point at infinity, and by the tag `1`
followed by the encodings of its two affine coordinates otherwise.
-/
noncomputable def encodePoint : I.E.toAffine.Point → List ℕ
  | .zero => [0]
  | .some (x := x) (y := y) _ => 1 :: (I.encodeElem x ++ I.encodeElem y)

/-- The point at infinity is encoded by the single tag `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 11 14 68]
theorem encodePoint_zero : I.encodePoint 0 = [0] :=
  rfl

/--
The list of natural numbers describing an input: the prime `p`, the degree `n` of `f`, the `n`
lower coefficients of `f` (the leading coefficient is `1`), the coefficients `a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄, a₆`
of the Weierstrass equation of `E`, and the two points `P` and `Q`.
-/
noncomputable def toNatList : List ℕ :=
  [I.p, I.f.natDegree] ++ (List.range I.f.natDegree).map (fun i => (I.f.coeff i).val) ++
    I.encodeElem I.E.a₁ ++ I.encodeElem I.E.a₂ ++ I.encodeElem I.E.a₃ ++ I.encodeElem I.E.a₄ ++
    I.encodeElem I.E.a₆ ++ I.encodePoint I.P ++ I.encodePoint I.Q

end Input

/--
A list of natural numbers is written over the standard Turing machine alphabet `Γ'` by writing
each number in binary (via `Computability.encodeNat`, least significant bit first) followed by a
`comma`.
-/
def encodeNatList (l : List ℕ) : List Γ' :=
  (l.map fun k => (encodeNat k).map Γ'.bit ++ [Γ'.comma]).flatten

/-- The list `[0, 1, 2]` is encoded as `, 1 , 01 ,` (least significant bit first). -/
@[category test, AMS 68]
theorem encodeNatList_example :
    encodeNatList [0, 1, 2] = [.comma, .bit true, .comma, .bit false, .bit true, .comma] := by
  have h2 : (2 : ℕ) = ((Num.pos (PosNum.bit0 1) : Num) : ℕ) := rfl
  have h1 : (1 : ℕ) = ((Num.pos 1 : Num) : ℕ) := rfl
  have h0 : (0 : ℕ) = ((Num.zero : Num) : ℕ) := rfl
  simp only [encodeNatList, List.map_cons, List.map_nil, encodeNat, h2, h1, h0, Num.of_to_nat]
  rfl

/-- The binary encoding of an input, over the alphabet `Γ'`. Its length is `Θ(log q)`. -/
noncomputable def Input.encode (I : Input) : List Γ' :=
  encodeNatList I.toNatList

/--
A time bound `T : ℕ → ℕ` is *sub-exponential* if `T n = 2 ^ o(n)`, that is, if for every
`ε > 0` we have `T n ≤ 2 ^ (ε * n)` for all sufficiently large `n`.
-/
def IsSubexponential (T : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (T n : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ (ε * n)

/-- Polynomial time bounds are sub-exponential. -/
@[category test, AMS 68]
theorem isSubexponential_pow (d : ℕ) : IsSubexponential fun n => n ^ d := by
  intro ε hε
  have h := isLittleO_pow_exp_pos_mul_atTop d (mul_pos hε (Real.log_pos one_lt_two))
  filter_upwards [tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop.eventually (h.bound one_pos)] with n hn
  simp only [Real.norm_eq_abs, one_mul, abs_pow, Nat.abs_cast] at hn
  push_cast
  calc (n : ℝ) ^ d ≤ |Real.exp (ε * Real.log 2 * n)| := hn
    _ = 2 ^ (ε * n) := by
      rw [abs_of_pos (Real.exp_pos _), Real.rpow_def_of_pos two_pos]
      ring_nf

/-- The exponential time bound `2 ^ n` is not sub-exponential. -/
@[category test, AMS 68]
theorem not_isSubexponential_two_pow : ¬ IsSubexponential fun n => 2 ^ n := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := (h (1 / 2) (by norm_num)).exists_forall_of_atTop
  have h1 := hN (N + 1) (by omega)
  have h2 : ((2 : ℝ) ^ ((1 / 2 : ℝ) * ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ))) < 2 ^ ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) :=
    Real.rpow_lt_rpow_of_exponent_lt one_lt_two (by push_cast; linarith)
  rw [Real.rpow_natCast] at h2
  push_cast at h1 h2
  linarith

/--
**Elliptic curve discrete logarithms in sub-exponential time.**

Can a discrete logarithm on an elliptic curve be computed in sub-exponential time?

That is, is there a deterministic Turing machine `M` and a sub-exponential time bound
`T n = 2 ^ o(n)` such that for every prime `p`, every finite field `𝔽_q = 𝔽_p[X]/(f)` with `f`
monic irreducible, every elliptic curve `E` over `𝔽_q` given by a Weierstrass equation and all
points `P`, `Q` of `E(𝔽_q)` with `Q` in the subgroup generated by `P`, the machine `M`, started
on the binary encoding of `(p, f, E, P, Q)`, halts within `T (input length)` steps and outputs
the binary encoding of a natural number `k` with `Q = k • P`?

The input length is `Θ(log q)`, so the generic algorithms, which take about `√q` steps, are
exponential. Only the worst-case running time of deterministic (classical) machines is
considered; randomised algorithms are not modelled, and Shor's algorithm solves the problem in
polynomial time on a quantum computer.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 14 68]
theorem discrete_logarithm_2 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (M : TM2ComputableAux Γ' Γ') (T : ℕ → ℕ), IsSubexponential T ∧
      ∀ I : Input, (∃ k : ℕ, I.Q = k • I.P) → ∃ k : ℕ, I.Q = k • I.P ∧
        Nonempty (TM2OutputsInTime M.tm (I.encode.map M.inputAlphabet.symm)
          (some (((encodeNat k).map Γ'.bit).map M.outputAlphabet.symm)) (T I.encode.length)) := by
  sorry

end DiscreteLogarithm2

items: Computation model: deterministic Turing machines in Mathlib's `TM2` model (`Turing.FinTM2`, `TM2OutputsInTime`), bundled with alphabet equivalences via `TM2ComputableAux Γ' Γ'`, exactly as `FormalConjectures/Millenium/PvsNP.lean` does. Randomized (Las Vegas / expected-time) algorithms, which the cryptographic literature often allows, are NOT modelled: Mathlib has no probabilistic TM primitives. This is recorded in the theorem docstring; a randomized variant is a distinct question.

Sub-exponential time is taken in the standard complexity-theoretic sense `T(n) = 2^{o(n)}`: `∀ ε > 0, T n ≤ 2^(ε n)` for all large `n` (definition `IsSubexponential`). This is the sense used for factoring/DLP (e.g. L_q[α, c] with α < 1 is 2^{o(n)}); the stricter alternative `∀ ε, T n ≤ 2^{n^ε}` was not used. One uniform machine with one bound `T` is required (not one machine per ε).

Input size: the time bound is in the length of a fixed concrete encoding `Input.encode` over Mathlib's alphabet `Γ'`: the numbers p, deg f, the deg f lower coefficients of f, the five Weierstrass coefficients a₁,a₂,a₃,a₄,a₆ and the two points (tag 0 for the point at infinity, tag 1 followed by both coordinates otherwise), each number written in binary (`Computability.encodeNat`) followed by a comma; field elements are written via their canonical representative of degree < deg f (`AdjoinRoot.modByMonicHom`). The encoding is injective and of length Θ(log q); it contains only the instance data (no leak of k). Injectivity is not formally proved (it is not needed to state the problem, since `TM2OutputsInTime` is used directly rather than `TM2ComputableInTime` with a `FinEncoding`).

Finite fields: every finite field is presented as `AdjoinRoot f` with `f : (ZMod p)[X]` monic and irreducible, `p` prime (`Fact p.Prime`, `Fact (Irreducible f)` as instance fields). This covers all finite fields 𝔽_{p^n} (with n ≥ 1 automatic from irreducibility) up to isomorphism; restricting to monic `f` is without loss of generality over a field and is needed for the canonical representatives.

Elliptic curves: `WeierstrassCurve` with `[E.IsElliptic]` (nonsingular), i.e. a long Weierstrass equation, so characteristic 2 and 3 are covered; the group is Mathlib's `E.toAffine.Point` with its `AddCommGroup` structure. Every elliptic curve over a field is isomorphic to such a curve.

Discrete logarithm problem is stated as a promise problem: the machine is only constrained on inputs with `∃ k : ℕ, Q = k • P` (equivalently `Q ∈ zmultiples P` in the finite group); it may output any natural number `k` with `Q = k • P` (not necessarily reduced modulo the order of `P`), written in binary; the output must be exactly the canonical binary string (`encodeNat k`, least significant bit first) on the output stack, following Mathlib's `TM2ComputableInTime` convention.

`answer(True)` means a subexponential (classical, deterministic) algorithm exists; `answer(False)` means none exists. Brute force / generic algorithms take 2^{Θ(n)} steps so the statement is not trivially true; the `Input` type is nonempty and the encoding is injective so it is not trivially false.

Tests: `Input.encodePoint_zero`, `encodeNatList_example`, `isSubexponential_pow` (polynomial bounds are subexponential) and `not_isSubexponential_two_pow` are included as `@[category test]` sanity checks of the bespoke definitions.

reviewer_notes: Conventions fixed (all documented in the module and theorem docstrings): (1) Computation model: deterministic Mathlib `Turing.FinTM2` (as in FormalConjectures/Millenium/PvsNP.lean) with worst-case time; randomised (Las Vegas / Monte Carlo, expected-time) algorithms — the cryptanalytic literature's usual default — are NOT modelled because Mathlib has no probabilistic machine and a bespoke randomised model would carry a high risk of subtle error. Hence a randomised-only subexponential algorithm would answer the informal question positively but would not settle this formal statement; the formal statement is a (documented) stricter variant. Quantum algorithms are excluded by construction. (2) Sub-exponential means T(n) = 2^{o(n)} in the input length n (∀ ε > 0, eventually T n ≤ 2^{εn}), the sense in which L_q[α, c], α < 1, is subexponential; the stricter class ∩_ε DTIME(2^{n^ε}) was not used. (3) The input is a canonical encoding of (p, f, E, P, Q) with F_q = F_p[X]/(f), f monic irreducible, of length Θ(log q); constant-factor changes of n do not affect 2^{o(n)}. (4) Promise-problem reading: the machine is only constrained on instances with Q ∈ ⟨P⟩ (the source says nothing about other inputs). (5) Output: any natural k with Q = k • P (nsmul suffices in a finite group). Verdict on c01/c02 omissions: their objection (randomised expected-time cannot be modelled; deterministic is a potentially different question) is correct as far as it goes, but the decomposition table explicitly makes the model a convention the formalizer fixes, and the repository's own P vs NP file fixes the same deterministic TM2 convention, so a documented deterministic statement is shippable rather than a reason to reject. Final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
